what_happened: In job 94p9, the user corrected Athena's first reading before work began. The reading did not match what the user meant. The user restated two decisions from the last critique. First, the proof that a pause never kills a running job must use a real child process (such as a sleep) registered as a line's running job. The watcher is driven to a pause on that line, and the test asserts the process is still alive and its registry entry is unchanged. The step that runs "go" on an already dispatched job is dropped. Second, each job's forecast cost p90 must be read from its reading's forecasts and passed to the T3 check, so T3 can pause. The plan's text saying p90 is unused must be fixed.
cause: The reading is built from the request text alone. It does not carry over what the last critique settled for the same job family: how to demonstrate that pause never kills, and which data feeds the T3 check. Nothing compares a new reading with those earlier decisions or with the plan's own stated facts, such as the claim that p90 is unused. The user is the only carrier of the settled approach, so the same kind of correction comes back on each retry or follow-up.
prevention: When a job retries or follows an earlier job or critique, Athena records the settled decisions of that attempt (the demonstration method, data sources and dropped steps) as structured carry-over. The reading stage must be given them, and a check must confirm that the new reading covers each one or states why it differs, before the reading is accepted. This covers the whole class of readings that drop a prior attempt's result.
proposed_request: Make the reading stage carry over settled decisions on retried or follow-up jobs. When a job continues an earlier job or critique, store that attempt's settled decisions (the demonstration method, the data sources to use and the steps dropped) and give them to the reading stage. Before a reading is accepted, check that it includes each settled decision or states why it differs, and show any gap to the user. Show this with a test where a retry's reading omits a settled decision and is flagged, and one where the reading includes all of them and passes. Apply it first to the pause work: the pause test must start a real child process registered as a line's running job, drive the watcher to a pause and assert the process is alive and its registry entry unchanged. Each job's forecast cost p90 must be read from its reading's forecasts and passed to the T3 check.
